newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks seen down on liquidity, loan worries.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks seen down on liquidity, loan worries.

text.p: Thai stocks were seen declining on Tuesday amid investor concerns over tight liquidity in the money market and on requirements for financial institutions to set up reserves for non-performing loans, brokers said.

"Apart from the lack of fresh and positive news, investors are worried that liquidity in the money market would tighten due to current high interest rates," Samart Rusmeerojwong of James Capel Asia said.
" Retail investors are also concerned that profits of financial institutions would fall after the setting up of more reserves for non-performing loans," Samart said.
Banks and finance companies are required to disclose their non-performing loans to the central bank for the first time from the end of this month.

Investor jitters over the non-performing loans issue led to a heavy selling of bank and finance shares on Monday driving the SET index to close 4.05 points lower at 511.55 on 2.9 billion baht turnover.
